note: Opening the floor-plan editor on the live Habbo hotel, in a room the capturing account owns. One burst: the two requests leave in the same millisecond and both answers arrive 87 ms later. Header ids are AIR-1.0.31's and NOT the emulator target build's -- 2735 and 2597 resolve as composers _SafeCls_3885 and _SafeCls_2685, 2757 and 2959 as events _SafeCls_3157 and _SafeCls_2697 in com/sulake/habbo/communication/_SafeCls_2127.as -- so the evidence here is the order, the membership and the field values. WHAT IT SETTLES. (1) Opening the editor sends exactly two requests, GetRoomEntryTile then GetOccupiedTiles, and both carry an empty body: both composer classes return an empty message array and both packets are 2 bytes on the wire. (2) Each is answered by exactly one packet, and by nothing else; the hotel answered them in the reverse of the order they were asked, which is scheduling, not a contract. (3) RoomOccupiedTiles is a 4-byte count followed by two 4-byte integers per tile -- 246 bytes for 30 tiles -- which is what _SafePkg_2964/_SafeCls_4542.as reads and what this emulator already writes. They are not the single bytes the height map uses for the same coordinates. (4) RoomEntryTile is three 4-byte integers, x, y and dir (_SafePkg_2964/_SafeCls_2963.as), also what this emulator already writes; the hotel sent (4,4) facing 2. (5) The entry tile is absent from the occupied list and no tile appears twice. (6) The hotel's list is sorted by x then by y. This emulator scans its grid row-major and so emits the same set sorted by y then x; the client pushes the pairs into _reservedTiles[y][x] and never reads the order. NO DELTA: both features were at official_behavior unknown and both now match, structure and membership. WHAT IT DOES NOT SETTLE: which objects make a tile occupied. This is one room whose contents were not inventoried, so whether the hotel counts a rug, a wall item or a standing avatar cannot be read off it. This emulator counts the footprint of every floor item and nothing else. ON PAIRING: both requests leave before either answer arrives, so positional pairing would hand both answers to GetOccupiedTiles and read GetRoomEntryTile as unanswered. Neither happened, and each answer carries a respondsTo saying which request it is for -- read off the payloads, which are unambiguous here (one is a tile list, the other three coordinates).
